mechanism_narrative: The sustained four-week recovery in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -22.4% to -13.3%, indicates a strong underlying momentum towards increased out-of-home activity, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent shift of PARKS mobility into positive territory (from -14.4% to 5.6%) and its continued increase suggests a growing public comfort with outdoor activities, which will spill over into other leisure and retail activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility crosses above 0% baseline and sustains growth for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite PARKS mobility remaining positive and growing, indicating a decoupling of outdoor leisure from retail spending.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and sustained increase in both WORKPLACES (from -17.0% to -11.3%) and TRANSIT (from -37.1% to -26.6%) mobility signifies a broader return to daily routines, including commuting and office presence, which directly increases foot traffic to retail and recreation venues during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases or stagnates, despite continued increases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, suggesting that increased commuting is not translating into retail spending.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 9.0% to 5.1%) indicates that people are spending progressively less time at home, a trend that reflects increased out-of-home activities and will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next two weeks as people seek more leisure and shopping opportunities.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases, even as RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to fall, indicating that reduced time at home is not being allocated to retail and recreation.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES mobility indices strongly suggests an ongoing easing of public health restrictions, which will continue to facilitate and encourage out-of-home activities, leading to a further increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:broad-based recovery across multiple mobility indices
failure_condition: A reversal or stagnation in the upward trend of at least three of the four specified mobility indices, coupled with a decline in RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 28 days, even if GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable and positive, indicating that essential activity does not translate to leisure spending.

candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility shows a consistent decline for at least three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases or stagnates, despite a continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, breaking the expected inverse correlation.
